flashcard_questions.q: Who suspects that Macbeth ‘play’dst most foully for’t’ at the start of Act Three?
What is a soliloquy in a play?
flashcard_questions.a: A speech where a character speaks their thoughts aloud, usually alone on stage.

flashcard_questions.q: Which adjective does Macbeth use for the crown the witches placed on his head?
What does the ‘barren sceptre’ image reveal about Macbeth’s reign?
flashcard_questions.a: His kingship will produce no heirs, so his line ends with him.

flashcard_questions.q: What has Macbeth given away when he speaks of his ‘eternal jewel’?
flashcard_questions.a: His soul, handed to the Devil, ‘the common enemy of man’.

flashcard_questions.q: Which darkly ironic instruction does Macbeth give Banquo before the banquet?
What is subtext in a character’s speech?
flashcard_questions.a: The underlying meaning behind the words, rather than their literal meaning.

flashcard_questions.q: Which line shows Lady Macbeth feels being queen has brought her nothing?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘Nought’s had, all’s spent, where our desire is got without content.’

flashcard_questions.q: Which metaphor does Macbeth use for his tormented mind in Act Three, Scene Two?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘O, full of scorpions is my mind, dear wife!’

flashcard_questions.q: Which Act One term of address does ‘dearest chuck’ replace?
What does Macbeth mean by ‘We have scotch’d the snake, not kill’d it’?
flashcard_questions.a: The threat to his power is only wounded: Banquo and Fleance are still alive.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the turning point of a tragedy?
flashcard_questions.a: The point where the main character’s fortunes change decisively, usually for the worse.

flashcard_questions.q: What does Banquo’s ghost sitting in Macbeth’s seat symbolise?
flashcard_questions.a: Banquo’s line, not Macbeth’s, will finally hold the throne.

flashcard_questions.q: Which metaphor shows Macbeth believes he has gone too far to turn back?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘I am in blood Stepp’d in so far that, should I wade no more, Returning were as tedious as go o’er.’

flashcard_questions.q: Which proverb shows Macbeth accepting that murder breeds more murder?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘It will have blood; they say, blood will have blood.’

notes: 15 cards: 7 quotation-recall fronts, 3 quotation-to-effect (‘barren sceptre’, ‘eternal jewel’, scotch’d snake), 1 symbol-to-meaning (the ghost in the seat), 1 quotation-to-speaker (Banquo’s soliloquy), 1 single-word quotation word (‘fruitless’), 2 term-to-definition (soliloquy, turning point). Avoided repeating the existing ‘dearest chuck’ card by flipping it to the Act One contrast it replaces. Hecate and the Middleton attribution dropped as scholarship flavour; all quotations verbatim from the content.
